ARBITER main manuscript analysis

Download main analysis (Word)

Home · Main analysis · Supplement · Software · Study repository and reproduction

ARBITER separates model interpretation from executable rules for the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomised trials (RoB 2) and retains sources, answers and evidence for inspection. We compared its complete workflow with minimal prompting using the same reported model identifier and identical supplied files for 102 trials from 16 reviews. Two human reviewers independently rated all 510 domain cells before viewing labels. Their assessments are labeled Human Review 1 and Human Review 2. A separate conditional label-choice analysis used 60 agreed choices among 80 arm disagreements; 20 choices split.

Results

The benchmark included 102 trials from 16 reviews and 510 domain cells after exclusion of three unsupported designs (Figure 3; Table 2). Both human reviewers independently assessed every cell.

Against Published across all 510 cells, exact agreement is 386/510 (75.7%) for ARBITER versus 395/510 (77.5%) for Direct prompting, a paired difference of −1.8 points (95% CI, −5.1 to 1.6).

Human Review 1: ARBITER 371/510 (72.7%) versus Direct prompting 332/510 (65.1%); paired gain 7.6 (5.1–10.2) percentage points. Human Review 2: ARBITER 433/510 (84.9%) versus Direct prompting 400/510 (78.4%); paired gain 6.5 (3.5–9.4) percentage points. Figure 4 shows absolute levels and paired gains, with the largest observed gains in D5. D3 remains strongly reference-dependent: ARBITER matches 43/102 ratings from Human Review 1 and 80/102 from Human Review 2. The human reviewers agree on 54/102 D3 cells.

Conditional blinded-label choices favored ARBITER in 53/60 agreed choices (88%; 95% CI, 80–96%). These 60 agreed choices arose from 80 arm-cells where the two arms disagreed, with 20 split choices. Review-specific and split-loss sensitivities are in Table 4.

Figure 5 distinguishes five-level from collapsed signalling-answer agreement on paired eligible components. In D3 against Human Review 1, the five-level difference is −10.3 points (95% CI, −17.2 to −3.2), whereas the collapsed difference is +8.5 (3.5–13.7), both on 165 components. D5 collapsed gains are +11.3 points for Human Review 1 and +3.7 (−0.3 to 7.4) for Human Review 2. eTable 4 retains source-specific domain summaries, eligibility accounting and complete paired question contrasts for both codings, including sparse and unfavorable results.

Table 3 reports process conformance and computational resources. All 510 ARBITER domain outputs reproduce from the rule engine; Direct prompting has 65/509 evaluable rule breaks (26 contradictory ratings and 39 required-question omissions). In separate structural checks, all 1538 active required answers cite evidence; 1407/1407 text spans and 14 image records are source-bound, and 102 bundles pass structural verification. These checks do not establish semantic support.

Median (IQR) runtime is 7.6 (6.1–10.5) versus 0.5 (0.4–0.5) minutes per trial, with a paired mean difference of 11.0 (95% CI, 8.4–14.1) minutes. API list-price equivalents are US$3.78 (3.46–4.10) versus US$0.09 (0.07–0.13), with a paired mean difference of US$3.68 (3.61–3.75). Human time and expenditure were not measured.

Reproduction

The study repository contains the analysis pipeline, test suite, numerical exports and output verifier. Supplementary methods and results provide supporting estimates, complete paired question results, prompts, reporting locations and links to the complete worked-example records. Trial PDFs are not redistributed.
